item.title: Draft full revision of basic guidelines for long-term care insurance benefit planning
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare published a draft full revision of the basic guidelines for smooth implementation of long-term care insurance benefits on 2026-11-26, with a stated comment deadline of 2026-12-26 00:00 JST. Based on Article 116(1) of the Long-Term Care Insurance Act, the draft would guide municipal and prefectural plans for fiscal years 2027–2029, including medium- and long-term service-demand estimates, consideration of elderly housing capacity, and service provision planning toward 2040. It proposes consideration of special regional home-care services in mountainous and depopulating areas, stronger medical-care coordination, and monitoring of residential fee-based homes for older people, including resident protection and concerns about steering residents toward particular services. Other proposed measures cover consultation support for older people without family support, dementia policies, business-continuity planning for community comprehensive support centers, and prefectural workforce, productivity and management-improvement initiatives. The outline schedules issuance of the Notice for late January 2027 and application from 2027-04-01; these are proposed dates, not confirmation of issuance or commencement. item.title: Draft banking ordinance, capital adequacy notice and supervisory guideline amendments
item.description: AI summary: The Financial Services Agency announced draft amendments on 2026-11-18 for public comment to the Regulation for Enforcement of the Banking Act, prudential notices and supervisory guidelines, allowing consolidation of subsidiary funds in proportion to ownership interests. The proposals would establish Pillar 3 disclosure provisions and notifications and forms for starting or suspending proportional consolidation, and clarify that leverage, liquidity and total loss-absorbing capacity (TLAC) rules use the same consolidation scope as capital adequacy calculations. They would also update domestic-standard banks' disclosure forms for items whose transitional measures have expired and adjust provisions defining internationally active banks in notices applicable to bank holding companies. Similar amendments are planned for specified non-bank financial institutions. The supplied excerpts do not establish a comment deadline or commencement date. item.title: FSA announcement on financing facilitation and business support
item.description: AI summary: On November 19, 2026, the Financial Services Agency held discussions with government officials and financial-sector representatives, and the government issued a request to financial-sector associations and related bodies. The request asks public and private financial institutions to provide attentive cash-flow support ahead of year-end and fiscal year-end, avoid mechanical lending decisions based solely on financial results, borrowing or past loan modifications, and respond promptly and flexibly to restructuring and refinancing requests. It also calls for tailored disaster-related support, including for those affected by the 2026 Kumamoto earthquake, and early management support coordinated with other lenders and business-support organizations. The excerpts additionally address possible cash-flow effects on agricultural, forestry and fisheries producers, food businesses and restaurant operators from proposed temporary food and beverage consumption-tax reductions for fiscal years 2027 and 2028; they do not establish that those reductions have been enacted. This is a government request, not an announcement of a new Act or ordinance.
